title: Latent Laplace Diffusion for Irregular Multivariate Time Series
claim: A conditioned reverse process denoises a latent trajectory in a Laplace-domain pole space, mirroring a forward corruption chain.
layout: Single panel, top-to-bottom conditioning then left-to-right; forward chain along the bottom
description: A wide diagram with three horizontal bands. At top left, a small plot of irregular multivariate time series with shaded gaps feeds into a blue-outlined 'History Summarizer' box. An arrow leads to the conditioning embedding E_t, shown as three rows of colored token blocks: green port tokens, purple dynamics tokens and yellow temporal tokens. Below, a 'Reverse Process' equation with the denoiser and its modal predictor and synthesizer branches into four arrows. These point to four complex-plane scatter plots (Re/Im axes) linked by arrows and ellipses. The blue poles start as diffuse noise and gradually organize into a clean curved arc. At the bottom, a forward-process chain of circled nodes runs from z_0 (clean) to z_T (noisy), right to left. At left, blue labeled boxes mark 'Latent Laplace Space' and 'Latent Trajectory', with up and down arrows for the maps L_θ and L_θ^+.
caption: Overview of the proposed Latent Laplace Diffusion. The observed history Hti is summarized into a conditioning token sequence Eti. The forward diffusion corrupts the clean latent trajectory from z0 to zT . In the reverse process, modal predictor Lθ estimates modal parameters and modal synthesizer L+
abstract: Irregular multivariate time series impose a trade-off for long-horizon forecasting: discrete methods can distort temporal structure via re-gridding, while continuous-time models often require sequential solvers prone to drift. To bridge this gap, we present Latent Laplace Diffusion (LLapDiff), a generative framework that models the target as a low-dimensional latent trajectory, enabling horizon-wide generation without step-by-step integration over physical time. We guide the reverse process utilizing a stable modal parameterization motivated by stochastic port-Hamiltonian dynamics, and parameterize its mean evolution in the Laplace domain via learnable complex-conjugate poles, enabling direct evaluation over irregular timestamps. We also link continuous dynamics to irregular observations through renewal-averaging analysis, which maps sampling gaps to effective event-domain poles and motivates a gap-aware history summarizer. Extensive experiments show that LLapDiff improves over baselines in long-horizon forecasting, and its continuous-time generative nature supports missing-value imputation by querying the same model at historical timestamps. Code is available at https://github.com/pixelhero98/LLapDiffusion.
